metadata.title: Nvidia Q2 earnings: stock surges 8.7%, adds $442 billion in value

content.text:
Nvidia added $442 billion to its market value on Thursday, the second-largest one-day gain by any stock in history, after the company's fiscal second-quarter results and revenue outlook eased investor concerns about the durability of artificial intelligence demand.
Nvidia stock climbed 8.7% on the day, a magnitude of gain the company had not seen since April 2025. Only Microsoft's $450 billion advance last month stands above it, according to Bloomberg. Nvidia, the largest company in the world, carries a market valuation of around $5.5 trillion.
The results broke a pattern in which Nvidia stock had fallen after each of the previous four earnings reports, despite meeting or beating estimates in each of those quarters. A large share of options traders had positioned for the stock to decline again following Wednesday's report.
The company said it expects revenue to grow roughly 70% in fiscal 2028, which runs from February 2027 to January 2028, well above analyst expectations of around 45% growth, according to Bloomberg. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang said demand "is much greater than 70%," but that the company is constrained by the amount of product it can supply. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress confirmed the 70% growth guidance on Wednesday.
JPMorgan wrote that the outlook likely remains conservative, as it "explicitly characterized the outlook as supply-constrained, with unconstrained demand pacing materially higher."
Huang declared that AI "reached its inflection point," adding that a far wider range of companies now depend on large clusters of graphics processing units than before. "Today, we have a golden age of new AI labs and startups, multiple frontier labs scaling in parallel, a thriving open-model ecosystem and physical AI coming online," he said.
Nvidia's ACIE segment — comprising AI Clouds, industrial, and enterprise customers — brought in $40.3 billion during the quarter, a 138% year-over-year jump, underscoring that the company is drawing revenue from a broader set of buyers than just major cloud platforms.
To put Thursday's $442 billion increase in context, only a small number of companies in the entire S&P 500 carry a total market value that large. Before Microsoft eclipsed it last month, Nvidia itself owned the record, having tacked on $440 billion in a single session after a 90-day tariff pause was announced in April 2025. Nvidia additionally owns the ignominious record for the steepest single-day market value destruction, with close to $600 billion disappearing in one session after China's DeepSeek AI model rattled investors.
Nvidia's results lifted broader markets Thursday. The S&P 500's information technology sector gained 3.4%, pushing the broad index up 0.7%. The Nasdaq composite rose 1.6% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed 0.2%.
